blocks.x: The working definition of Process & Task Mining at Dataq Software: scope we sign, the cadence you can plan around, platform evidence generated in-flight, and outcomes measured against your baseline.

Automating an imagined process is how programs waste their first year. We mine the truth from system event logs and desktop telemetry: variant analysis showing the twelve real paths where the process map shows three, bottleneck heatmaps by team and system, rework loops, and conformance gaps against policy. Task mining adds the human layer — application switching, copy-paste bridges, swivel-chair work — quantifying exactly where minutes bleed.

The output is a ranked automation portfolio with evidence: each candidate scored on frequency, variance, fragmentation and value, with a target-state design for the top flows. Clients use this as the foundation for agentic programs and as a continuous instrument post-deployment, comparing actual execution against design drift every quarter.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
